transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-05-21
Start: 15:30 PT
Duration: 48 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Aaron Chen (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Sharma (FinOptima, Lead ML Eng), John Park (CTO), Leah Gomez (SRE)

Summary (auto): Quick console walkthrough focused on tracing, request logs, and error analysis. Customer wants to understand debugging flows, per-request timelines, and how Redwood surfaces regressions and anomalous latencies. Discussed Dedicated vs Hosted for pilot and security compliance needs.

Topics: tracing, request logs, error analysis, per-route dashboards, KMS/SOC2, pilot/benchmarks

[00:00] Aaron Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'll hand off to maya to run through the console tracing flows, i'm on audio but maya will demo the UI.
[00:16] Maya Patel: cool, hey priya, john, leah, good to meet you. i'll share screen, let me know if the stream is choppy. (screen share noise) so first thing, quick context: tracing in the console links request logs to model traces, token timings, and error reasons. you can search by trace id, user_id or route.
[00:37] Priya Sharma: sounds good, we mostly care about p95 latency spikes and request failures that cause LLM hallucinations or truncations. we run a heavy prefix cache, and we want to know when the KV cash (sic) is missed.
[00:55] Maya Patel: yeah — and sorry, KV cash, it's "KV cache" — console surfaces cache hit/miss per request. when it's a miss you'll see more decoding time in the trace.
[01:10] John Park: when you say trace, is that per-token times or just aggregate request timing?
[01:18] Maya Patel: both — we show an overall timeline, plus a token timing waterfall for the last 256 tokens in the request. the waterfall is approximate for streaming responses (there's some alignment noise in transcription).
[01:33] Leah Gomez: can you show a failure example? like 500s or rate-limit errors and where stack traces sit?
[01:41] Maya Patel: yep, open this request log, i'll filter to errors. see here: trace id 8f3a2b. this one errored during decode, console shows an error bucket "decode OOM" with a stack snippet and the agent-suggested remediation (retry at lower max_tokens or route to a lower-quant model).
[02:05] [02:06] Priya Sharma: that stack snippet looks generic - is the snippet always exact? sometimes we need original host logs for deeper debugging.
[02:12] Aaron Chen: good point — we include a trace pointer you can click to see the backend node id and request headers; for Dedicated or Private you can configure extended log retention or ship logs to your SIEM.
[02:28] Maya Patel: right, for Private deployments you can also enable full VM/node-level logs. in hosted mode we retain standardized traces and audit logs for X days depending on plan.
[02:42] John Park: that's helpful. on encryption - KMS integration, can we use our own key?
[02:48] Aaron Chen: yes, Dedicated and Private support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM). we'll share the KMS integration doc after the call.
[02:58] Maya Patel: back to tracing — here's the per-route dashboard. you can see model-level p50/p95, and a cost per request breakdown. notice this spike here — if we click into the trace, we see it was a large prompt with cache miss plus a heavy reranking step.
[03:22] [03:24] Priya Sharma: reranking — is that a Redwood feature or our app layer? we do rerank client-side today.
[03:30] Maya Patel: it's usually your app, but we surface per-step annotations for things like post-processing or reranking. you can tag steps in the request metadata so traces show them.
[03:40] Leah Gomez: about observability, does Redwood export traces to our existing tracing backend? we use Jaeger and Datadog.
[03:46] Maya Patel: yes, we support sending traces and request metrics to Datadog/Prometheus and we can push spans to Jaeger for Private deployments. hosted customers often use webhook ingestion for specific events.
[03:58] John Park: what about RBAC and audit logs for who viewed traces? our security team requires strict access controls.
[04:05] Aaron Chen: console has RBAC and SSO (SAML/OIDC). audit logs record trace access and changes; we can increase retention and push to your SIEM for compliance.
[04:18] Priya Sharma: i saw in your docs something about automatic regression alerts tied to evals — can you show that quickly?
[04:25] Maya Patel: sure — open the "quality" tab. we run evals against your prompt set and can create alerts on metric deltas. for example if embedding similarity or response length drops past a threshold we'll flag it and link to failed traces and example requests.
[04:40] [04:41] Priya Sharma: helpful. in our environment we get intermittent timeouts that coincide with autoscaler thrashing — can Redwood traces show contention on the GPU side?
[04:52] Maya Patel: yes-ish — in Dedicated we surface node-level metrics like GPU utilization, queue depth, and batching windows. for hosted we expose per-request queue time and batch size. if you see high queue wait the trace will show "queued for X ms" and batch size at the time.
[05:10] John Park: can we set alerts for increased queue wait or batch size > N?
[05:14] Maya Patel: yep, alerts are configurable per-route. you can set thresholds on p95, queue time, batch size, error rate.
[05:22] Leah Gomez: curious about interactive debugging — say we replay a request in your sandbox to reproduce a bug. is that possible?
[05:28] Maya Patel: we have a replay tool. with trace id you can replay the request in the console sandbox or download the payload. for privacy, replay on hosted is scrubbed unless you opt into extended retention; Dedicated/Private can replay exact payloads if you enable that.
[05:44] Priya Sharma: what's the cost implication of extended retention and replay?
[05:50] Aaron Chen: retention is an add-on for hosted; Dedicated includes configurable retention in the reserved capacity contract. replay itself is low cost but storing full payloads and extended retention increases storage charges. we'll include an example price table.
[06:05] [06:06] Priya Sharma: timeline wise, we want to run a pilot in prod-like traffic in June. our blockers are SOC2 evidence and VPC peering rules to test Dedicated.
[06:17] Aaron Chen: understood. we can fast-path SOC2 pack and start a firewall/VPC checklist with Leah. Dedicated provisioning for a pilot typically takes 2-3 weeks once the contract is signed.
[06:29] Leah Gomez: we also need KMS/HSM proof-of-concept and the ability to route requests to a fallback model during outages. how does Redwood handle graceful degradation?
[06:41] Maya Patel: grace degradation is built-in: smart routing can fallback to cheaper or lower-latency variants. you can configure automatic fallback policies — e.g., if latency > 800ms, route to a smaller quantized model. console shows the fallback events and associated traces so you can audit quality regression.
[06:59] Priya Sharma: can you show a real fallback event?
[07:02] Maya Patel: sure, filter to route=fallback-example. here's trace 2b9c... see the cascade: primary model timed out, request retried to fallback, and console links both traces side-by-side with diffed outputs.
[07:20] John Park: neat. question on model versions — can traces tie to a specific model build or quantization profile?
[07:27] Maya Patel: yes, each trace records model_id, model_version, and quantization profile; the console allows pinning a version per-route and shows rollout status for canary and A/B tests.
[07:38] [07:40] Priya Sharma: we do heavy evals nightly; will the console surface regression alerts from those evals automatically?
[07:46] Maya Patel: you can hook your eval pipeline or use Redwood Optimize to schedule evals. if an eval fails we create an incident with linked traces and affected prompts.
[07:56] Leah Gomez: security: does the console show which user inspected a trace? we need who/what for audits.
[08:02] Aaron Chen: yes — audit logs include actor, action (viewed trace/replayed request/changed policy), and timestamp. those are exportable.
[08:12] Priya Sharma: any gotchas around PII in traces? we scrub headers by default, right?
[08:18] Maya Patel: by default hosted traces are redacted; you can opt into full payload capture with explicit consent and retention settings. Private/Dedicated gives you full control over redaction.
[08:31] [08:33] John Park: competitor question: how do you compare to Anthropic/OpenAI in terms of debugging UX?
[08:39] Aaron Chen: we focus on production observability tied to inference economics and rollouts. compared to general APIs we provide trace-to-cost linkage, rollout controls, and built-in fallback policies oriented for production apps.
[08:55] Priya Sharma: sounds promising. question about request logs export: can we stream them to our S3 bucket for longer retention?
[09:02] Maya Patel: yes, for Dedicated/Private we can forward to your S3 or GS bucket; hosted supports scheduled export or webhook/streaming to partner storage.
[09:14] [09:15] Aaron Chen: quick demo switch — i'll show the per-request timeline UI: here you can see client RTT, queue time, kernel time, token decode time, and network time. the timeline has clickable spans and you can open a flame graph for batched requests.
[09:33] Priya Sharma: flame graph — does that include kernel-level breakdown? we need to know if it's a kernel or memory stall.
[09:40] Maya Patel: kernel-level breakdown is available in Dedicated; hosted shows a logical breakdown (compilation, kernel exec, decode) but not raw kernel traces.
[09:50] Leah Gomez: ok, that works. any limitations around request sampling? like do you sample traces or all requests?
[09:57] Maya Patel: by default we sample at 1% for full traces and keep aggregated metrics for all. for pilot/Dedicated we can increase sampling to 100% or implement conditional sampling on error/latency.
[10:10] Priya Sharma: good — we'll want 100% sampling for the first week of pilot.
[10:15] Aaron Chen: noted. next steps — i'll send pricing and the security pack; maya will drop the recording and sandbox link. priya/leah you'll share traffic and firewall constraints. we'll schedule a deep dive to run the benchmark.
[10:28] [10:30] John Park: one more Q: if we hit a quality regression after a model rollout, can console automatically rollback?
[10:36] Maya Patel: you can configure automatic rollback rules tied to eval metrics or p95 latency. console can execute a rollback or pause rollout and notify stakeholders.
[10:45] Priya Sharma: awesome. thanks, this was really useful.
[10:48] Aaron Chen: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the docs.

(End of 48-min call approx)

Notes: Transcript shows occasional ASR miscues (KV cash/KV cache) and some speaker overlap. Action items captured above.
